executivePulse.interpretation: Memory and AI infrastructure remain under high pressure. Server DRAM and HBM are currently among the most strained areas. The daily check on 2026-08-15 confirmed a material change in the situation. New capacity and improved yields can provide relief, but will reach the market only with a time lag. For buyers, supply assurance, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain decisive.

signals.title: HBM does not solve the memory wall: Gelsinger and SK hynix seek the post-HBM architecture
signals.summary: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger called HBM at the RAISE Summit technically unsatisfactory but the best currently available memory solution for AI. He pointed to heat generation in stacked DRAM, limited interface bandwidth and disadvantages in bit-, power- and bandwidth-efficiency. SK hynix vice-president Kim Ho-sik partially agreed: HBM is not the final answer to the memory wall. SK hynix is therefore investigating other approaches to the memory bottleneck; at the same time HBM remains the most practical solution today.
signals.analysis: This signal does not weaken the HBM-shortage thesis but separates two time horizons: Short term HBM remains RED → because AI platforms continue to rely on HBM, advanced packaging and scarce DRAM wafers. Long term the competition shifts from individual memory products to the co-design of compute, memory, packaging and interconnect. No new supply relief emerges for server DRAM or procurement in the near term.
signals.source: Maeil Business Newspaper – HBM is lousy, former Intel CEO taunts
